title: California Labor Code section 2699 - Private Attorneys General Act civil actions and penalties
claims: Section 2699(a) provides that any provision of the Labor Code that provides for a civil penalty to be assessed and collected by the Labor and Workforce Development Agency may, as an alternative, be recovered through a civil action brought by an aggrieved employee on behalf of the employee and other current or former employees against whom a violation of the same provision was committed, pursuant to the procedures in Section 2699.3.

Section 2699(c)(1) defines aggrieved employee as any person who was employed by the alleged violator and personally suffered each of the violations alleged during the period prescribed under Section 340 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Section 2699(f)(2)(A) sets a default civil penalty, where the person employs one or more employees, of one hundred dollars for each aggrieved employee per pay period, with lower figures for specified wage statement violations and a fifty dollar figure where the violation resulted from an isolated, nonrecurring event not extending beyond the lesser of 30 consecutive days or four consecutive pay periods.

Section 2699(f)(2)(B) sets the civil penalty at two hundred dollars for each aggrieved employee per pay period if, within the five preceding years, the agency or any court found the employer's policy or practice giving rise to the violation unlawful, or if the court determines the employer's conduct was malicious, fraudulent, or oppressive.

Section 2699(g) provides that if, before receiving the notice of violation or a request for records, the employer had taken all reasonable steps to be in compliance with all provisions identified in the notice, the recoverable civil penalty shall not be more than 15 percent of the penalty sought, and section 2699(h) provides a cap of 30 percent where the employer takes all reasonable steps to prospectively comply within 60 days after receiving the notice; neither cap applies to penalties recovered under subdivision (f)(2)(B).

Section 2699(g)(2) and (h)(2) provide that all reasonable steps may include, but are not limited to, periodic payroll audits with action taken in response, dissemination of lawful written policies, training supervisors on applicable Labor Code and wage order compliance, and appropriate corrective action with regard to supervisors, and that the existence of a violation despite the steps taken is insufficient to establish that an employer failed to take all reasonable steps.

Section 2699(k)(1) provides that any employee who prevails in an action shall be entitled to an award of reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and that nothing in the part limits an employee's right to pursue or recover other remedies available under state or federal law, separately or concurrently.

Section 2699(m) provides that, except as provided in subdivision (n), civil penalties recovered by aggrieved employees shall be distributed 65 percent to the Labor and Workforce Development Agency and 35 percent to the aggrieved employees.

Section 2699(s)(2) provides that the superior court shall review and approve any settlement of any civil action filed pursuant to the part, and that the proposed settlement shall be submitted to the agency at the same time it is submitted to the court.

Section 2699(v) provides that the amendments made by the act adding that subdivision apply to a civil action brought on or after June 19, 2024, and not to an action in which the required notice under Section 2699.3 was filed before June 19, 2024.

Section 2699(i) provides that an aggrieved employee shall not collect a civil penalty for any violation of Sections 201, 202, or 203, or for a violation of Section 204 that is not willful or intentional, or a violation of Section 226 that is not knowing or intentional or a failure to provide a wage statement, that is in addition to the civil penalty collected by that aggrieved employee for the underlying unpaid wage violation.

Section 2699(k)(2) provides that no action shall be brought under the part for any violation of a posting, notice, agency reporting, or filing requirement of the code, except if the filing or reporting requirement involves mandatory payroll or workplace injury reporting.
Section 2699(n) provides that civil penalties recovered under paragraph (1) of subdivision (f) shall be distributed to the Labor and Workforce Development Agency.
Section 2699(o) provides that the penalty recovered pursuant to the part shall be reduced by one-half if the employees' regular pay period is weekly rather than biweekly or semimonthly.

Section 2699(r) provides that nothing in the part is intended to alter or otherwise affect the exclusive remedy provided by the workers' compensation provisions of the code for liability against an employer for the compensation for any injury to or death of an employee arising out of and in the course of employment.
notes: Fetched 2026-09-30 from the publisher's own site and read in full. Last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026; the section was substantially rewritten by the 2024 reform whose transition rule is subdivision (v), so older descriptions of PAGA penalty amounts and distribution may not match this text. Section 2699.3 (the notice procedure) and Code of Civil Procedure section 340 (the period) were not read for this record, so no notice deadline or limitation period is stated from them. Subdivision (d) (cure), (i) (no stacking of certain penalties on the underlying wage penalty), (j) and (l) were read but are summarised only where a claim states them.
